title: Counit transpose of a compatible coefficient refinement map
statement: For adjunctions L₁ ⊣ R₁ and L₂ ⊣ R₂, functors S and T, and a natural transformation c : S ⋙ L₂ ⟶ L₁ ⋙ T, a commuting square c.app M ≫ T.map h₁ ≫ δ₁ = L₂.map δ₂ ≫ h₂ implies the corresponding square after transposing h₁ and h₂, with the mate of c and R₂.map δ₁.

source.place: 6.7.6–6.7.7, coefficient supplement, counit calculation used in the final refinement square

proof.text: Apply the inverse Hom bijection for the second adjunction. Use right and left naturality of the two Hom equivalences to move δ₁ and δ₂ outside the transposes. The mate counit formula rewrites the middle term as L₂.map (S.map (adj₁.homEquiv h₁)) followed by c and the first counit. Naturality of c and functoriality of T combine the first counit with h₁, and the assumed commuting square gives the result.

theorem refinement_coefficient_mate
    {C₁ : Type u₁} {D₁ : Type u₂} {C₂ : Type u₃} {D₂ : Type u₄}
    [Category.{v₁} C₁] [Category.{v₂} D₁]
    [Category.{v₃} C₂] [Category.{v₄} D₂]
    {L₁ : C₁ ⥤ D₁} {R₁ : D₁ ⥤ C₁} {L₂ : C₂ ⥤ D₂} {R₂ : D₂ ⥤ C₂}
    (adj₁ : L₁ ⊣ R₁) (adj₂ : L₂ ⊣ R₂)
    {S : C₁ ⥤ C₂} {T : D₁ ⥤ D₂} (c : S ⋙ L₂ ⟶ L₁ ⋙ T)
    {M : C₁} {N : D₁} {M' : C₂} {N' : D₂}
    (h₁ : L₁.obj M ⟶ N) (h₂ : L₂.obj M' ⟶ N')
    (δ₁ : T.obj N ⟶ N') (δ₂ : S.obj M ⟶ M')
    (h : c.app M ≫ T.map h₁ ≫ δ₁ = L₂.map δ₂ ≫ h₂) :
    S.map (adj₁.homEquiv _ _ h₁) ≫
        (mateEquiv adj₁ adj₂ (TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _ c)).natTrans.app N ≫ R₂.map δ₁ =
      δ₂ ≫ adj₂.homEquiv _ _ h₂
